primitives.name: Process trace
primitives.desc: Cryptographic process-trace library: schemas, hashing, Merkle trees, bundles and selective disclosure — the Proof-of-Intent core.

primitives.name: Materios anchor client
primitives.desc: Blob upload through the gateway (body-bound, single-use upload signatures), receipt submission, certification polling, Merkle proofs and end-to-end receipt verification against Materios.

primitives.name: Cardano anchor client
primitives.desc: Direct Cardano L1 anchors: Proof-of-Intent label 2222 and Materios checkpoint label 8746 submitters and verifiers, with a chained submit queue so one wallet never double-spends its own change and each dedupe key is answered by the one tx that reached the chain.

primitives.name: Orynq anchor registry (Midnight)
primitives.desc: Compact contract (compactc 0.31.1) that records orynq anchors on Midnight with a maintenance authority of committee [], threshold 1, counter 0, so no update can ever apply. anchor(commitment, kind) refuses kind 2; anchor_hiding(attribute) computes a SHA-256 hiding commitment in-circuit from a private opening and binds the attribute to that commitment, not to the trace; neither reads state. Pure circuits author_key, entry_digest, hidden_digest, hiding_commitment and derive_salt are plain SHA-256. compile.sh --check reproduces the committed managed/ byte for byte with compactc from tools/compactc, which pins every file of the release by sha256 and installs only into directories that no one but the caller can write or swap out: every directory above them is owned by the caller or root and closed to group and others, and nothing is installed below a shared sticky directory such as /tmp. The same installer puts the DUST spend circuit's prover key, verifier key and zkir (dust/9, k=13, pinned as midnight-ledger 8.1.3 pins them) beside the k=13/14 parameters, the whole of what a registry transaction proves with.

primitives.name: GRANDPA finality and strict inclusion verifier
primitives.desc: Decides from untrusted grandpa_proveFinality and chain_getHeader answers (batched JSON-RPC) whether a block is final, trusting only given checkpoints: it follows each authority set change from the nearest checkpoint below the block (the outgoing set's supermajority-signed justification of a set-change block whose header hashes to it and names the next set in FRNK; forced and delayed changes refused), then checks the finalizing set's justification and the header chain down to the block. Cost is bounded by maxSetChanges (default 2016, six weeks of 30-minute sets, about 6.7 KB each), never by chain age. Inclusion is a strict decode: the ordered-trie (layout V1) extrinsicsRoot of the body and exactly one bare Midnight.send_mn_transaction(tx) extrinsic, never a byte search. Golden vectors from Midnight mainnet and preprod; Materios, also a GRANDPA chain, can verify against it.

primitives.name: Signed KNOWN_AUTHORS document
primitives.desc: orynq-known-authors/v1: the author keys a Midnight anchor verifier recognizes, each with a role (relay) and an inclusive window of block heights, plus the GRANDPA finality checkpoints it trusts, as a JSON string signed with Ed25519 by an offline trust-root key over a domain-separated message. Parsing is strict (unknown fields, networks, roles and overlapping windows refused). Revocation is a higher-serial document closing a key's window, so no verifier scans the permissionless registry; the highest serial wins and an older one never rolls a revocation back. scripts/known-authors.ts creates the root key and signs documents offline. No root or document ships until deci signs the first.

primitives.name: Midnight anchor toolkit
primitives.desc: verifyMidnightAnchor checks an anchor from the transaction's own bytes: hash binding first, then exactly one registry call whose guaranteed transcript equals the compiled circuits' op for op, the node's block (hash, header, extrinsicsRoot, known runtime, strict send_mn_transaction inclusion), GRANDPA finality from a signed or caller checkpoint, the registry's pinned deploy verified the same way, the request's expectation and a KNOWN_AUTHORS author window; statuses invalid, conflict, unavailable, unverified-finality, unauthenticated, author-revoked and valid, which exists only at consensus-verified assurance; verifiedFields name only what the commitment binds (kind 2: committedAttribute, never the trace). findMidnightAnchors lists an author set's anchor candidates in a window of at most 20,000 blocks from the indexer's contractActions subscription (WebSocket, credential in a header), decoding each from its own bytes, bounded by maxActions with a resumable cursor. It also computes commitments with the compiled contract's own pure circuits (entryCommitment, hiddenDigest, hidingCommitment, deriveSalt, authorKey), writes and reads random author key files only their owner can read, lists the deployed registry generations per network (none yet) with their pinned verifier keys and runtime, reads a Midnight indexer and node through midnightSource (Blockfrost endpoints with the project id read from an owner-only file and kept out of every error), builds registry calls for a given network from the compiled circuits (unprovenRegistryCall), serves each file of the committed build only while it matches contract/HASHES.txt (compiledContractFile), frames a transaction as the bare Midnight.send_mn_transaction extrinsic a node accepts (midnightExtrinsic, the inverse of the strict inclusion decode), and builds the registry's exact deploy state from the compiled constructor and the sha256-pinned verifier keys, and refuses anything else: assertImmutableAuthority (committee [], threshold 1, counter 0), assertRegistryState (operations, canonical verifier keys, schema) and assertRegistryDeployBytes, which decodes the exact deploy bytes before or after proving and requires the initial state byte for byte. Private until the mainnet registry exists.

primitives.name: Write-ahead anchor submission journal
primitives.desc: SQLite (node:sqlite) journal for anchor submissions, exported as anchors-midnight/journal: one live attempt per anchor key, the attempt's row written with the hash computed from its final bytes before they are broadcast, so a broadcast that times out after acceptance or a process that dies around it is answered by txHash and never sent twice; a row whose broadcast never returned is resent with the same bytes; pending rows retire only on the indexer's report or when the indexer's newest block passes the TTL plus a margin (chain time, not the local clock). reconcile(chain) settles every pending row by txHash alone after a restart, preparing and broadcasting nothing. Serialized per journal; across processes the second writer never broadcasts. For the Midnight submit package and the signer.

primitives.name: Midnight anchor submitter
primitives.desc: Deploys the immutable orynq-anchor-registry and writes anchors to it. openWallet runs a wallet-sdk 1.2.0 WalletFacade (HD account 0 index 0) that refuses a mnemonic deriving other than the recorded addresses, pays fees from DUST only, proves in a worker thread with zkir-v2 from sha256-pinned key material (registry circuits from the committed build, the DUST spend and k=13/14 parameters from the installer's directory; nothing fetched), saves and restores its sync state in an owner-only file, and reaches Blockfrost through a loopback relay that adds the project-id header so the credential never sits in a URL the SDK logs. registryDeployer prepares the final balanced bytes, refuses them unless they deploy exactly the registry's initial state, and submits them through the write-ahead journal at most once per network; registryOperator writes kind-1 anchor and kind-2 anchor_hiding calls under an author key read only from a 0600 file (salts derived from a salt key, openings returned only to the caller), checks the final bytes decode to exactly the intended anchor before broadcast, broadcasts the bare Midnight.send_mn_transaction over JSON-RPC, and waits by txHash. Every submission first checks the runtime is 1000300. scripts/deploy-mainnet.ts is the fail-closed mainnet preflight (chain name and genesis, runtime, recorded wallet, DUST floor, exact summary) that sends only after deci types a token bound to the bytes' transaction hash at an interactive terminal, and refuses in any agent-driven process. Private until the mainnet registry exists.

primitives.name: PoI anchor worker

primitives.name: npm release
primitives.desc: Publishes every workspace package version npm lacks on a push to main: a token-less step installs, runs release-guard (refuses a public package with a runtime dependency on a private one, named directly, through an npm: or workspace: alias or by a workspace: path resolved through symlinks, or on a local path (link:, file: or bare) or a spec npm-package-arg cannot classify, a version npm would record differently, and a version below one npm already has by npm's semver order, prereleases included), then builds and packs them (scripts/pack-unpublished.mjs, the choice changeset publish makes); only the digest-pinned npm-publish plugin, named by the npm_token secret's image filter, holds the token; post-publish-check then installs each published version from npm, alone and together, imports it and requires one copy of each WASM singleton.
